correctness.rationale: For all \(p\ge1\) and all rank-one projector pairs, phase alignment and span reduction give the exact scalar \(G_p\). A strict monotone weighted-average ratio proves the unique critical angle or the bisector maximum, with correct equality at \(c=1-1/p\). The endpoint cases \(c=0,1\) and all maximizing rays were reconstructed. The Euclidean closed form follows from an exact quadratic optimization and its branch derivatives; the standalone verifier returned the documented success marker. No finite test is promoted to an infinite-dimensional proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating abstract, the 2024 full-text two-operator inequalities and 2023 full-text p-joint moment work were compared by claimed implication. The two accessible primary papers neither state nor imply the sharp \(c=1-1/p\) optimizer-count threshold with the Euclidean algebraic branch. Multiple semantic and alias searches found no covering indexed result. The motivating article body could not be accessed, so equivalence elsewhere remains a real stated risk rather than a false certainty.

value.rationale: The smallest noncommuting positive operator pair has an exact symmetry-breaking phase boundary in two continuous parameters, a complete optimizer classification, and a rational Euclidean branch with genuine differentiability loss. This clarifies equality structure missing from general joint-radius inequalities and is a natural benchmark, not an arbitrary coordinate slice.
